title: Normal delivery
stem: Birth room. Mrs Lai, 28, is at 39 weeks in her second pregnancy. The pregnancy has been normal. The head is crowning. There are no complications. Conduct the delivery and the third stage.

phases.title: Prepare
phases.goal: Two teams, the pack, warmth, and oxytocin drawn up.

phases.title: Deliver the baby
phases.goal: A controlled delivery of the head, the cord, the shoulders.

phases.title: A&E nurse
phases.goal: Recognise imminent birth and do the nurse's job while the midwife delivers.

notes:
A normal birth with no complication. Hands on: a pad guards the perineum and a palm keeps the head flexed. As the head crowns she pants rather than pushes, so it is born slowly. Feel for a nuchal cord and ease a loose loop over the head. Wait for restitution. With the next contraction, gentle axial traction for the anterior shoulder, then the posterior, never hard. Onto her abdomen skin to skin, note the time, dry the baby, and swap the wet towel for a dry one and a hat.

Third stage, after NICE NG235 and QS105: feel for a second twin, then oxytocin 10 IU intramuscular, then clamp the cord no sooner than 1 minute and before 5 minutes. Wait for separation: a gush of blood, the cord lengthening, the fundus rising. Controlled cord traction with the other hand guarding the uterus. Twist the membranes out. Check the placenta, the membranes and three cord vessels. Rub the fundus, look for tears, and measure the blood loss.

script.say: Neonatal nurse for the baby; one person stays with Mrs Lai. PPE; sterile delivery pack with two clamps and scissors. Warm towels, hat, resuscitaire on.
Oxytocin 10 IU drawn up for the third stage.

Pad guarding the perineum, my palm on the head to keep it flexed; as it crowns, 'pant, don't push'. Feel for a cord: a loose loop slips over the head. Wait for restitution. With the next contraction, gentle downward axial traction for the anterior shoulder, then upward for the posterior. Onto mum's tummy skin to skin; time of birth; dry her, dry towel and hat; check breathing, tone and colour.

Feel the abdomen: no second twin; oxytocin 10 IU IM. After at least 60 seconds, clamp and cut the cord. Wait for separation: a gush of blood, the cord lengthening, the fundus rising. Controlled cord traction with my other hand guarding the uterus above the pubis; twist the membranes out. Check the placenta, membranes and three cord vessels; the fundus firm; tears; measured blood loss.
